## L1
1. Q: What comes next? 15, 20, 25, 30, ? | Choices: 40, 35, 31 | Correct: 35 | Why: The numbers go up in 5s, so after 30 comes 35.
2. Q: What comes next? 18, 20, 22, 24, ? | Choices: 26, 24, 25 | Correct: 26 | Why: Every jump is 2, so the count carries on past 24 to 26.
3. Q: What comes next? 40, 50, 60, 70, ? | Choices: 71, 90, 80 | Correct: 80 | Why: Counting in 10s from 70 gives 80.
## L2
1. Q: What comes next? 7, 10, 13, 16, ? | Choices: 19, 22, 18 | Correct: 19 | Why: The step is +3, so 16 + 3 = 19.
2. Q: What comes next? 120, 113, 106, 99, ? | Choices: 93, 85, 92 | Correct: 92 | Why: The numbers drop by 7 each time, and 99 − 7 = 92.
3. Q: What comes next? 0, 9, 18, 27, ? | Choices: 45, 36, 37 | Correct: 36 | Why: The step is +9, so 27 + 9 = 36.
## L3
1. Q: Find the missing number: 7, ?, 19, 25 | Choices: 13, 31, 14 | Correct: 13 | Why: 25 − 19 = 6 is the step, so the blank is 19 − 6 = 13.
2. Q: Find the missing number: 40, ?, 64, 76 | Choices: 51, 52, 88 | Correct: 52 | Why: The step is 76 − 64 = 12, and 64 − 12 = 52.
3. Q: Find the missing number: 91, ?, 97, 100 | Choices: 103, 95, 94 | Correct: 94 | Why: The step is 3, so the blank is 91 + 3 = 94.
## L4
1. Q: What comes next? 3, 6, 12, 24, ? | Choices: 27, 48, 96 | Correct: 48 | Why: Each number is double the one before, so 24 × 2 = 48.
2. Q: What comes next? 7, 14, 28, 56, ? | Choices: 112, 84, 63 | Correct: 112 | Why: Doubling 56 gives 112 — the gaps double as well: 7, 14, 28, 56.
3. Q: What comes next? 160, 80, 40, 20, ? | Choices: 18, 5, 10 | Correct: 10 | Why: Each number is half the one before, and half of 20 is 10.
## L5
1. Q: Which rule makes 4, 7, 10, 13? | Choices: Add 4 each time, Add 3 each time, Multiply by 2 each time | Correct: Add 3 each time | Why: Every gap is 3, and doubling would make 4, 8, not 4, 7.
2. Q: Which rule makes 5, 10, 15, 20? | Choices: Multiply by 2 each time, Add 5 each time, Add 4 each time | Correct: Add 5 each time | Why: Doubling fits 5 → 10 but then wants 20, not 15; the gaps are all 5.
3. Q: Which rule makes 2, 10, 18, 26? | Choices: Add 8 each time, Multiply by 5 each time, Add 9 each time | Correct: Add 8 each time | Why: 2 × 5 = 10 works once, but every gap is 8, so the rule is add 8.
## L6
1. Q: in → out: 1→8, 2→11, 3→14, 6→? | Choices: 33, 23, 18 | Correct: 23 | Why: Out rises 3 for each 1 of in and 1 → 8, so out = 3 × in + 5, and 3 × 6 + 5 = 23.
2. Q: in → out: 2→10, 3→14, 4→18, 9→? | Choices: 38, 22, 36 | Correct: 38 | Why: The rule is × 4 then + 2, so 4 × 9 + 2 = 38.
3. Q: in → out: 3→13, 4→15, 5→17, 10→? | Choices: 20, 72, 27 | Correct: 27 | Why: The rule is × 2 then + 7, so 2 × 10 + 7 = 27.
## L7
1. Q: What comes next? 5, 6, 8, 11, ? | Choices: 12, 15, 16 | Correct: 15 | Why: The gaps are 1, 2, 3, so the next gap is 4: 11 + 4 = 15.
2. Q: What comes next? 2, 4, 8, 14, ? | Choices: 22, 16, 20 | Correct: 22 | Why: The gaps grow 2, 4, 6, so the next gap is 8 — it is not a doubling pattern: 14 + 8 = 22.
3. Q: What comes next? 12, 15, 19, 24, ? | Choices: 29, 27, 30 | Correct: 30 | Why: Gaps 3, 4, 5 make the next gap 6, and 24 + 6 = 30.
## L8
1. Q: What comes next? 2, 5, 10, 13, 26, ? | Choices: 52, 29, 39 | Correct: 29 | Why: The rules alternate +3, ×2, +3, ×2, so the next one is +3: 26 + 3 = 29.
2. Q: What comes next? 4, 9, 27, 32, 96, ? | Choices: 101, 37, 160 | Correct: 101 | Why: +5 and ×3 take turns, and the last step was ×3, so now add 5: 96 + 5 = 101.
3. Q: What comes next? 15, 17, 34, 36, 72, ? | Choices: 108, 144, 74 | Correct: 74 | Why: +2, ×2, +2, ×2 — a doubling is always followed by an add: 72 + 2 = 74.
## L9
1. Q: The pattern starts 5, 8, 11, … What is the 20th term? | Choices: 60, 62, 65 | Correct: 62 | Why: After the 5 there are 19 steps of 3: 5 + 19 × 3 = 62.
2. Q: The pattern starts 2, 9, 16, … What is the 15th term? | Choices: 100, 105, 107 | Correct: 100 | Why: After the 2 there are 14 steps of 7: 2 + 14 × 7 = 100.
3. Q: The pattern starts 12, 16, 20, … What is the 31st term? | Choices: 136, 124, 132 | Correct: 132 | Why: After the 12 there are 30 steps of 4: 12 + 30 × 4 = 132.
## L10
1. Q: The pattern is 5, 8, 11, 14, … Which rule gives term n? | Choices: 2n + 3, 3n + 2, 3n + 5 | Correct: 3n + 2 | Why: The terms rise 3 at a time, so the rule starts 3n; 3 × 1 = 3 and term 1 is 5, so add 2.
2. Q: The pattern is 1, 5, 9, 13, … Which rule gives term n? | Choices: 4n − 3, 4n + 1, 3n + 4 | Correct: 4n − 3 | Why: The step is 4, and 4 × 1 = 4 is 3 more than term 1, so subtract 3.
3. Q: The pattern is 14, 19, 24, 29, … Which rule gives term n? | Choices: 5n + 14, 9n + 5, 5n + 9 | Correct: 5n + 9 | Why: The step is 5, and 5 × 1 = 5 needs 9 more to reach the first term 14.
